title: 4 things every coding course needs so students finish
sources: Jordan (2015), IRRODL: MOOC completion rates decrease as course length increases
Lally et al. 2010 (habits form with consistency)
teyro.app/teach: four-step lessons (Learn, Apply, Reflect, Deepen); creators keep 70% (80% Founding)

lines.text: Four things every coding course needs, | so students *actually* finish.
First, *short* lessons. | When researchers compared online courses, | the *longer* the course, | the *fewer* people finished.
Second, practice that's *checked instantly.* | Testing yourself beats rereading, | and feedback nearly *doubles* the benefit.
Third, a moment to *explain it back.* | Putting an idea in your *own words* | shows what you *actually* understood.
And finally, a reason to come back *tomorrow.* | Habits come from showing up *most days,* | so streaks and reminders *matter.*
So in our Studio, every lesson runs in *four* steps: | learn, | apply, | reflect, | and deepen.
If you teach coding or AI, | you keep *seventy percent* of every payment. | Go to teyro dot app slash *teach.*
